chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty:
"No mother should be harmed because of her child, nor a father because of his child."

He said, "The wet nurses would send one of them to the man when the man desired intercourse. She would say, 'I will not let you go; I fear that I will become pregnant and kill this child of mine whom I am nursing.' And when the wife called the husband, he would say, 'I fear that I will have intercourse with you and kill my child.' So he would leave her and not have intercourse with her. So Allah forbade that, so that the man would not harm the woman and the woman would not harm the man."
ai.seo_question: What is the historical context of the Quranic verse 'La tudaar walidatun bi-waladiha' regarding wet nurses and marital relations?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates that the verse addresses the pre-Islamic practice where wet nurses and husbands abstained from marital relations due to the mistaken belief that sexual fluids or exertion would harm the nursing infant. This mutual harm (darar) prompted divine prohibition, establishing that marital intimacy does not invalidate breastfeeding rights, thereby balancing conjugal rights with maternal care in Shia jurisprudence.
